original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-properties-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. The category $\QCoh(S_\etale, \mathcal{O})$
of quasi-coherent modules on $S_\etale$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item The kernel and cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
\item Given a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
if two out of three are quasi-coherent so is the third.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$
is of finite presentation.
then the internal hom
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is quasi-coherent.
\end{enumerate}
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $S$ be a scheme, and let $\operatorname{QCoh}(S_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\mathcal O)$ denote quasi-coherent modules on its small étale ringed site. This category has the following closure properties (where exactness, colimits and internal Hom are taken in the ambient category of site modules): (1) arbitrary direct sums and (2) arbitrary colimits are quasi-coherent; (3) kernels and cokernels of morphisms between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (4) in a short exact sequence of site modules, if any two of the three terms are quasi-coherent, so is the third; (5) tensor products of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; (6) if $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent and $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation, then $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is quasi-coherent.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves six closure properties of QCoh modules on SMALL étale site: arbitrary sums/colimits, kernels and cokernels, two-out-of-three, tensor, and internal Hom when first factor finitely presented. This retains stronger SMALL-site kernel property.

hypotheses: Quasi-coherent modules on the small étale ringed site of a scheme.
conclusions: Listed closure properties for sums, colimits, kernels/cokernels, extensions, tensor products and finite-presentation internal Hom.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-properties-quasi-coherent-on-big}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
The category $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_\tau, \mathcal{O})$
of quasi-coherent modules on $(\Sch/S)_\tau$
has the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Any direct sum of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item Any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent.
\item The cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent sheaves
is quasi-coherent.
\item Given a short exact sequence of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
if $\mathcal{F}_1$ and $\mathcal{F}_3$ are quasi-coherent so is
$\mathcal{F}_2$.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
the tensor product is quasi-coherent.
\item Given two quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules
$\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{G}$ such that $\mathcal{F}$
is finite locally free, the internal hom
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
is quasi-coherent.
\end{enumerate}
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
On these ringed sites, "quasi-coherent" denotes the locally presented $\mathcal O$-modules of the site (equivalently those in the essential image of $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^a$ in the situations below). The quasi-coherent $\mathcal O$-modules on the big site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ are closed under arbitrary direct sums, arbitrary colimits, cokernels of maps among them, extensions (if the outer two terms of a short exact sequence are quasi-coherent, so is the middle), and tensor products. If $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent and $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free, then $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ is quasi-coherent. Unlike the small-étale assertion, this statement does NOT assert arbitrary ambient kernels or arbitrary finitely-presented internal Hom are quasi-coherent on the big site.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves six closure properties on BIG τ sites, carefully restricting the claim to cokernels but NOT general kernels, extensions from outer terms, tensor, and internal Hom only for finite locally free first factor.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-qc-colimits}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The category $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
has colimits and they agree with colimits in the categories
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, and
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\item Given $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ in $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
the tensor products $\mathcal{F} \otimes_\mathcal{O} \mathcal{G}$
computed in $\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, or
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$ agree and the common value
is an object of $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\item Given $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$ in $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$
with $\mathcal{F}$ finite locally free (in fppf, or equivalently \'etale, or
equivalently Zariski topology) the internal homs
$\SheafHom_\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})$
computed in $\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, \mathcal{O})$,
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_\etale, \mathcal{O})$, or
$\textit{Mod}((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$ agree and the common value
is an object of $\QCoh((\Sch/S)_{fppf}, \mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $S$ be a scheme. For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ consider the big ringed site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ and its associated category of $\mathcal O$-modules; identify a quasi-coherent module on each site by the common pullback-section rule $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,f^*\mathcal F_S)$ from a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. (1) The category $\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}},\mathcal O)$ has all colimits; their images under each of the three associated-site inclusions agree with the ambient module-category colimits. (2) For any two such quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, their tensor products computed in the big Zariski, étale and fppf module categories agree and are quasi-coherent. (3) If additionally $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free (equivalently for the Zariski, étale and fppf topologies), then the internal Hom sheaves $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ computed in these three big site module categories agree and are quasi-coherent.
stage_b_review_note: Retains all three cross-topology claims for quasi-coherent big-fppf modules: ambient colimits agree in Zariski/étale/fppf, tensor agrees for qc pairs, and internal Hom agrees when first factor finite locally free in each topology.
